newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl's CDU falls behind SPD in Allensbach poll. [CORRECTED 12:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Kohl's CDU falls behind SPD in Allensbach poll. [CORRECTED 12:30 GMT]

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's ruling coalition is slipping further behind the opposition Social Democrats as voters blame the government for high unemployment and stagnation, an opinion poll published on Wednesday said.

The respected Allensbach Institute said Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) and Bavarian sister party CSU would receive the backing of just 33.2 percent of the voters, down from 33.8 percent a month ago and from 36.5 percent in February -- the last time Kohl's party lead the Social Democrats (SPD).
The next election is due in September 1998 (Corrects from September 1997). Germany's unemployment has reached post-war records this year and is currently around 11 percent.

The SPD, meanwhile, gained a full percentage point to 37.6 in the last month, according to the monthly Allensbach survey taken from June 18 to June 30. That was up from 35.5 percent in February and the highest level of backing for Germany's main opposition party since 1993.

"The continued high unemployment and the blockade of political reforms through the SPD-dominated upper house of parliament are raising a sense of paralysis and stagnation in the population," said Renate Koecher, in an article accompanying the survey in the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung newspaper.
"The voters are holding liable those in office who should be taking action," Koecher added. "The governing parties are in a popularity trough at the moment."

But the Free Democrats (FDP) that share power as the junior partner in Kohl's centre-right government were clearly on an uptrend. The FDP has campaigned aggressively for lower taxes and drawn the ire of Kohl's CDU on several occasions.
The FDP was up to 6.4 percent compared to 6.0 percent last month and 5.0 percent in February.
The Greens, who would likely form a coalition with the SPD, were slightly lower in the latest Allensbach survey at 13.5 percent compared to 14.0 percent last month.
In the last general elections in October 1994, the CDU and CSU won a combined 41.5 percent and the FDP won 6.9 percent. The SPD had 36.4 percent and the Greens 7.3 percent.
